readme:
# 39. SDPO Top-K 与尾部概率散度

将词表压缩成学生 top-k 项和一个尾部桶，保留分布的总概率质量。

## 论文与范围

[Reinforcement Learning via Self-Distillation](https://arxiv.org/html/2601.20802v2) · Appendix A.3: Top-K KL Divergence · [Code](https://github.com/lasgroup/SDPO)

实现 top-k 选择、尾部 logsumexp 和 reverse KL；测试与信息损失曲线已提供。

## 接口

### 返回值要求

按下列结构返回，保留形状中的单例维度。标量 Tensor 的形状为 `()`，不是 Python `float`。

#### `topk_tail_reverse_kl` · 需要实现

返回浮点 Tensor `divergence`，形状为 `student_logits.shape[:-1]`，从 `[..., V]` 中 **只移除词表轴**。因此 `[B, L, V]` 返回 `[B, L]`，`[V]` 返回标量 `()`。每项是 student top-`k` token 与剩余 tail bin 上的反向 KL（`k=V` 为完整 KL）。保留 student 的 dtype/device 和梯度，teacher logits 固定；不对 batch/token 求平均。

### 公式与约定

```python
topk_tail_reverse_kl(student_logits, teacher_logits, k)
```

输入同形有限 logits [...,V]，V>0、k 为 [1,V] 中的 Python 整数。CPU float32/float64。输出 [...]，保持 dtype/device。支持非连续输入；教师不接收梯度。top-k 索引来自学生，两边使用完全相同的索引；并列值可使用 torch.topk 的任意确定结果。不要求对排序索引求梯度，但选中概率和尾部质量都要可微。

## 定义

令 I=TopK(p)，p_tail=sum_{v不在I}p_v，q_tail 同理。输出 `sum_{i in I} p_i log(p_i/q_i) + p_tail log(p_tail/q_tail)`。k=V 时省略尾部项。不能重新归一化 top-k 项；用补集 logsumexp 计算尾部 log mass，避免 1-sum(topk) 的消减误差。

## 例子

p=[0.6,0.25,0.15]，q=[0.3,0.2,0.5]，k=1：两桶为 p=[0.6,0.4]、q=[0.3,0.7]，KL≈0.19204。

## 小实验

五分类分布中逐步增加 k，画出粗粒度 KL 接近完整 KL 的曲线。本题仍接收完整 logits 来测试公式，未实现分布式词表通信或验证大模型显存收益。

T0 检查接口；T1 使用独立数值例子；T2 检查梯度与不变量；T3 在小实验中实际调用提交实现。

solution:
import torch


def topk_tail_reverse_kl(student_logits, teacher_logits, k):
    """Coarsen the vocabulary into student top-k tokens and one complementary bin."""
    if isinstance(k, bool) or not isinstance(k, int) or not 1 <= k <= student_logits.shape[-1]:
        raise ValueError("k must be an integer in [1, vocabulary_size]")
    s = student_logits.log_softmax(-1)
    t = teacher_logits.detach().log_softmax(-1)
    indices = s.topk(k, dim=-1).indices
    sp, tp = s.gather(-1, indices), t.gather(-1, indices)
    result = (sp.exp() * (sp - tp)).sum(-1)
    if k < s.shape[-1]:
        selected = torch.zeros_like(s, dtype=torch.bool).scatter(-1, indices, True)
        sl = s.masked_fill(selected, -torch.inf).logsumexp(-1)
        tl = t.masked_fill(selected, -torch.inf).logsumexp(-1)
        result = result + sl.exp() * (sl - tl)
    return result
notes:
# 参考思路

tail 是完整补集的一个桶，不是丢弃的剩余项。细化分区使 KL 不减，这是 T2 的独立信息论性质。k=V-1 时最后一个桶只有一个 token，因此已与完整 KL 相同。有限差分在无 top-k 排名变化的点验证梯度；极端 logits 检查数值稳定性。

en.title: SDPO Top-K and Tail-Mass KL
en.readme:
# 39. SDPO Top-K and Tail-Mass KL

Coarsen the vocabulary into student top-k entries and one tail bin while preserving total probability mass.

## Paper and scope

[Reinforcement Learning via Self-Distillation](https://arxiv.org/html/2601.20802v2) · Appendix A.3: Top-K KL Divergence · [Code](https://github.com/lasgroup/SDPO)

Implement top-k selection, complementary logsumexp, and reverse KL; tests and information curves are supplied.

## Interface

### Return requirements

Use the return structure below exactly; Tensor shapes include singleton dimensions. A scalar Tensor has shape `()`, not a Python `float`.

#### `topk_tail_reverse_kl` · Required

Return one floating Tensor `divergence`, shape `student_logits.shape[:-1]`: remove **only the vocabulary axis** from `[..., V]`. Thus `[B, L, V]` returns `[B, L]`, and `[V]` returns a scalar `()`. Each value is reverse KL for student top-`k` tokens plus the complementary tail bin (`k=V` gives full KL). Preserve student dtype/device and gradients; freeze teacher logits. Do not apply batch/token mean reduction.

### Formula and conventions

```python
topk_tail_reverse_kl(student_logits, teacher_logits, k)
```

Inputs are same-shaped finite logits [...,V], V>0, with Python integer k in [1,V]. Use CPU float32/float64; return [...] with preserved dtype/device. Support noncontiguous inputs and stop teacher gradients. Select indices from the student and use the same indices for both distributions. At ties any torch.topk selection is valid. Indices need no gradient, but selected probabilities and tail mass do.

## Definition

Let I=TopK(p), with p_tail and q_tail the complementary masses. Return `sum_{i in I} p_i log(p_i/q_i) + p_tail log(p_tail/q_tail)`. Omit the tail for k=V. Do not renormalize selected entries. Compute tail log mass with logsumexp over the complement to avoid cancellation in 1-sum(topk).

## Example

For p=[0.6,0.25,0.15], q=[0.3,0.2,0.5], k=1, the two bins are p=[0.6,0.4], q=[0.3,0.7], giving KL≈0.19204.

## Toy experiment

Increase k for a five-category distribution and plot coarse-grained KL approaching full KL. Full logits remain inputs to make the formula testable; this module does not implement distributed vocabulary communication or benchmark LLM memory savings.

T0 checks contracts, T1 independent numerical examples, T2 gradients and invariants, and T3 the submitted functions in the supplied experiment.
en.notes:
# Reference notes

The tail is one bin for the entire complement, not discarded probability. Refining a partition cannot decrease KL, giving an independent T2 invariant. At k=V-1 the tail contains one token, so the result already equals full KL. Finite differences use points with stable rankings; extreme logits check numerical stability.
